summary:
Mictocaris halope is a tiny crustacean found nowhere else on Earth but the silent, salt-dark waters of five anchialine caves beneath Bermuda's limestone parishes. Living in near-total isolation, deep within submerged cave passages barely connected to the open sea, it represents an entire taxonomic order unto itself — a lineage so ancient and singular it seems like a secret the ocean kept.

Its world is vanishingly small, and shrinking. Quarry blasting shakes the rock above one of its only homes. Cesspit sewage seeps toward others. Tourism presses in from all sides. With an area of occupancy of just one square kilometer, this creature exists on the edge of everything — asking almost nothing of the world, and receiving very little in return.
